recommendation: Drain the field to reduce humidity, avoid excess nitrogen fertilizer, and apply a copper-based bactericide (e.g. copper oxychloride) at early symptom onset.
pesticide_dosage: Copper oxychloride 50% WP — 2.5g per litre of water, sprayed every 7-10 days.
preventive_measures: Avoid overhead irrigation during the vegetative stage
Remove and destroy infected plant debris after harvest
biological_control: Apply Pseudomonas fluorescens as a seed treatment
Encourage field sanitation to reduce bacterial inoculum

recommendation: Apply a systemic fungicide such as tricyclazole at the first sign of lesions, and split nitrogen application to avoid lush, blast-prone growth.
pesticide_dosage: Tricyclazole 75% WP — 0.6g per litre of water, sprayed at 10-day intervals.
preventive_measures: Use blast-resistant rice varieties where available
Practice crop rotation with non-host crops
biological_control: Apply Trichoderma viride to the soil before transplanting
Use silicon-based soil amendments to strengthen plant cell walls

recommendation: Improve soil fertility with balanced NPK and potassium application, and apply a fungicide such as mancozeb or propiconazole if the infection is severe.
pesticide_dosage: Mancozeb 75% WP — 2.5g per litre of water, sprayed every 10-14 days.
preventive_measures: Correct soil nutrient deficiencies, especially potassium and silicon
Avoid water stress during grain filling
Ensure proper spacing for airflow between plants
biological_control: Apply Trichoderma harzianum as a seed and soil treatment
Incorporate organic matter to improve soil health

recommendation: No treatment is required. Continue standard field monitoring and good agronomic practices.
preventive_measures: Continue routine field scouting for early symptom detection
Maintain balanced fertilization and irrigation schedules

recommendation: Avoid excessive nitrogen and insecticide misuse that kills natural predators; apply a targeted insecticide such as buprofezin if populations exceed the economic threshold.
pesticide_dosage: Buprofezin 25% SC — 1ml per litre of water, sprayed at the base of the plant.
preventive_measures: Monitor populations regularly with light traps
biological_control: Conserve natural predators such as spiders and mirid bugs
Avoid broad-spectrum insecticides that harm beneficial insects

recommendation: Remove and destroy affected tillers (deadhearts/whiteheads), and apply a granular insecticide such as cartap hydrochloride if infestation is high.
pesticide_dosage: Cartap hydrochloride 4G — 20kg per hectare, applied to standing water.
preventive_measures: Synchronize planting dates across the area to break the pest cycle
Remove stubble after harvest to eliminate overwintering larvae
biological_control: Encourage natural predators such as birds and spiders
